summary: Steel tower recorded in Nipissing, Ontario, at 455 m (1493 ft) and named at Tower Lake, Eldee, on an undated still-standing list; the exact site is an admitted best guess.

facts.status_note: Named on an undated list titled Still Standing; its author keeps the list as it is and does not check it. A 2013 note says the MNR decided to remove many such towers. No source confirms the tower stands today.

evidence.supports: Planners usually chose a naturally high elevation for a tower
evidence.quote: Usually the best bet was to put an early warning tower on top of a naturally high elevation like a sloping hill.

notes_for_editor: Three things support the story: the Firelookout.ca record (steel tower, Nipissing location with a postal code, 455 m site elevation, and the contributor's own statement that the exact spot is a best guess), and two copies of the undated 'Ontario Fire Towers Still Standing' list, which place Garrow Tower at Tower Lake, Eldee, with no asterisk. The status was 'standing' before this check; that reading rested only on the undated list, whose author says it is kept as it is, so it is now 'unknown'. The list's author says it is being kept as it is, so it is not a current check, and the 2013 MNR note names no tower. No source gives a location for Eldee, so the Tower Lake place name has not been matched to the Firelookout coordinates (46.69811, -79.28098). A Facebook group post whose title reads 'Rip Nipissing tower' appeared in a search snippet only; the page could not be read, so it is not used and is a lead for a human to check. No build date, height, staffing, fire history or access rule was found. The Firelookout.ca record's contributor note means the site location is unverified. Confidence is low.
